> Also where is that property quarkus.kafka-streams.application-server defined? Is that a pass-through property, and if so, what's facilitating the pass-through?

It's a regular property, [defined](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/c7b990b0377a25cf9bcc09de9876c616fcd6f454/extensions/kafka-streams/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/kafka/streams/runtime/KafkaStreamsRuntimeConfig.java#L28) as a config item.
OK I think I understand what's happening.  The run time configuration properties are getting expanded, and they're expanding against the build time config.  It should be an easy(ish) fix though.

issue.title: Do not expand run time properties at build time
Simplify development of Kafka Streams applications

issue.body:
As of #2663, there's support for running Apache Kafka Streams stream processing applications on Quarkus. There's still some boilerplate, though, which could be further reduced. Eventually, all that the application developer should have to provide is the actual stream pipeline topology and its configuration. So I could see the following to be done as a follow-up:

- [x] Support that a `Topology` can be provided by the application developer using a producer method
- [x] Have the extension automatically take care of managing the `KafkaStreams` instance running that topology (start, stop)
- [x] Support configuring KS via `application.properties`, akin to messaging sinks/sources in Reactive Messaging (see https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/3030 for an issue related to resolving nested properties - as needed for resolving the application name - which should be fixed by now)
- [x] Take advantage of simpler JNI set-up (see https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/3060)

If have some code for this already handy in a PoC.

@gsmet, can you assign this to me?

body:
I wouldn't use `${hostname}` as that would often be undefined (on windows for example, the variable `COMPUTERNAME` is often used).  And the host name isn't necessarily a DNS-resolvable name.

You might want to make the default socket address be `${quarkus.http.host}:${quarkus.http.port}` instead, assuming you want it to be populated with the same address.
